text:
Maya R: Heads up — saw an off-by-one token when loading the llamaX-chat weights from s3 for staging, looks like a tokenizer/config mismatch.
Priya N: Ugh. Can you dump a minimal repro? path/weights + token counts? :eyes:
Maya R: s3://redwood-models/llamaX-chat/v1/weights.tar.gz; quick repro: prompt.encode("Hello") returns 3 tokens, but runtime generation prepends another <bos> so the effective input is 4 tokens.
Samir: That usually happens when the tokenizer has add_bos=True but our serving stack also inserts a BOS for chat templates. Are you using the chat template that includes a leading <bos>?
Maya R: Yep — model card had template like "<bos>{system}{user}". I think tokenizers from the model zoo set `add_bos_token=true` by default.
Priya N: Two options: remove <bos> from templates, or set tokenizer.add_bos_token=false in the model config so encode() stops adding it. Which is less risky?
Eva C: For backwards compatibility I'd prefer forcing templates to be neutral (no special tokens) and relying on the runtime to add BOS/EOS consistently. That way models that expect raw text don't get double tokens.
Tony L: Agree. Also watch pad/eos ids — I saw a case where eos_token_id=1 in the weights but our serving config expected 2, so post-processing trimmed an extra token.
Maya R: Repro log snippet: ```
# encoder
>>> tokenizer.encode("Hello")
[1, 234, 2]
# server prepends bos
> input_ids = [0] + [1,234,2]
```
Samir: We should add a pre-flight config validator that compares tokenizer.add_bos_token, eos_token_id, pad_token_id with the serving defaults. Quick check in model manifest would catch this.
Maya R: Filed a tiny PR with a validator and a test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/432 — it flags when both template contains <bos> and tokenizer.add_bos_token==true.
Priya N: Nice. Can you also add a lint rule that fails CI if chat template includes explicit special tokens like <bos> or <eos>? Those should live in runtime config, not templates.
Maya R: Yep added a lint commit in the PR. CI failing on one unrelated flake atm.
ci-bot: Build #2145 — tests: 102/107 passed. Failing: test_template_lint (flake).
Tony L: I'll pick up the flake. After CI green, can we schedule a rolling canary? Want to avoid mass rollout during peak infra window.
Samir: Canaries: default small percent routing + compare token counts & perplexity on the same prompt set. We'll also auto-fallback to last-known-good if token mismatch > 2 tokens.
Priya N: Ops question — where should we store the corrected tokenizer config? model_manifest.json next to weights?
Maya R: Yes: add `model_manifest.json` under the same s3 prefix with a `tokenizer_config` block. Example snippet I proposed: ```json
{
  "tokenizer_config": {
    "add_bos_token": false,
    "eos_token_id": 2,
    "pad_token_id": 0
  }
}
```
Eva C: Looks good. CI/test should read that and validate against runtime defaults during onboarding.
Maya R: Also updated the onboarding doc in the repo (docs/onboarding/tokenizer-guidelines.md) with examples of chat templates that are safe: start with plain system text (no special tokens).
Priya N: Quick code-review ping @Tony L and @Samir on the PR — it's small and blocks the canary. :rocket:
Tony L: On it, will review in next 30m.
Samir: Thanks — once merged I'll kick the canary and monitor token-length diffs and generation sanity.
Maya R: Thanks folks. If anyone hits other weird tokenization deltas please drop examples here (short snippets work). :thumbsup:
Infra Bot: Reminder — rolling canaries must be scheduled 02:00-05:00 UTC by policy.
Maya R: noted, scheduling for 03:00 UTC tomorrow.
Priya N: Thanks!
